article.title: Migratory Beekeeping
footer: Adapted from "America's Beekeepers: Hives for Hire" by Alan Mairson, National Geographic.

items.sentence_raw: To eke out a full-time living from their honeybees, about half the nation's 2,000 commercial beekeepers pull up stakes each spring, migrating north to find more flowers for their bees.
Besides turning floral nectar into honey, these hardworking insects also pollinate crops for farmers - for a fee.
As autumn approaches, the beekeepers pack up their hives and go south, scrambling for pollination contracts in hot spots like California's fertile Central Valley.
Of the 2,000 commercial beekeepers in the United States about half migrate.
This pays off in two ways.
Moving north in the summer and south in the winter lets bees work a longer blooming season, making more honey - and money - for their keepers.
Second, beekeepers can carry their hives to farmers who need bees to pollinate their crops.

Every spring a migratory beekeeper in California may move up to 160 million bees to flowering fields in Minnesota and every winter his family may haul the hives back to California, where farmers will rent the bees to pollinate almond and cherry trees.
Migratory beekeeping is nothing new.
The ancient Egyptians moved clay hives, probably on rafts, down the Nile to follow the bloom and nectar flow as it moved toward Cairo.

In the 1880s North American beekeepers experimented with the same idea, moving bees on barges along the Mississippi and on waterways in Florida, but their lighter, wooden hives kept falling into the water.
items.explain: Q25: The passage says early American beekeepers tried moving bees on barges but their hives *'kept falling into the water'* — this means the first attempts failed. So the answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: Other keepers tried the railroad and horse-drawn wagons, but that didn't prove practical.
Not until the 1920s when cars and trucks became affordable and roads improved, did migratory beekeeping begin to catch on.
For the Californian beekeeper, the pollination season begins in February.
At this time, the beehives are in particular demand by farmers who have almond groves; they need two hives an acre.
For the three-week long bloom, beekeepers can hire out their hives for $32 each.
It's a bonanza for the bees too.
Most people consider almond honey too bitter to eat so the bees get to keep it for themselves.
By early March it is time to move the bees.
items.explain: Q13: The passage says *'By early March it is time to move the bees'* and they do this *'at night'* — so beekeepers **'prepare'** for migration. The word **'prepare'** in the list matches this idea of getting ready to move. So the answer is **O**.

items.sentence_raw: It can take up to seven nights to pack the 4,000 or so hives that a beekeeper may own.
These are not moved in the middle of the day because too many of the bees would end up homeless.
But at night, the hives are stacked onto wooden pallets, back-to-back in sets of four, and lifted onto a truck.
items.explain: Q13: The passage says *'By early March it is time to move the bees'* and they do this *'at night'* — so beekeepers **'prepare'** for migration. The word **'prepare'** in the list matches this idea of getting ready to move. So the answer is **O**.

items.sentence_raw: It is not necessary to wear gloves or a beekeeper's veil because the hives are not being opened and the bees should remain relatively quiet.
items.explain:
Q13: The passage says *'By early March it is time to move the bees'* and they do this *'at night'* — so beekeepers **'prepare'** for migration. The word **'prepare'** in the list matches this idea of getting ready to move. So the answer is **O**.

Q14: The passage says the hives are not opened so the bees *'should remain relatively quiet'* — this means the hives are **'full'** of calm bees. The list word **'full'** connects to this state of being undisturbed. So the answer is **P**.

items.sentence_raw: Just in case some are still lively, bees can be pacified with a few puffs of smoke blown into each hive's narrow entrance.
items.explain: Q15: The passage says *'bees can be pacified with a few puffs of smoke'* — **'pacified'** means made calm, and **'smoke'** is the exact word from the list. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: In their new location, the beekeeper will pay the farmer to allow his bees to feed in such places as orange groves.
items.explain: Q16: The passage says *'the beekeeper will pay the farmer'* — but the question says farmers **'pay'** beekeepers. ***Watch the direction of payment*** — here the beekeeper gives money to the farmer, so the farmer receives a **'charge'** from the beekeeper. The list word **'charge'** fits this reversed money flow. So the answer is **F**.

items.sentence_raw: The honey produced here is fragrant and sweet and can be sold by the beekeepers.
To encourage the bees to produce as much honey as possible during this period, the beekeepers open the hives and stack extra boxes called supers on top.
These temporary hive extensions contain frames of empty comb for the bees to fill with honey.
In the brood chamber below, the bees will stash honey to eat later.
items.explain:
Q23: The diagram shows the bottom box — the passage says *'In the brood chamber below, the bees will stash honey'*. So the answer is **brood chamber**.

Q26: The passage says *'In the brood chamber below, the bees will stash honey to eat later'* — **'stash honey to eat'** means they keep it for themselves. So the answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: To prevent the queen from crawling up to the top and laying eggs, a screen can be inserted between the brood chamber and the supers.
items.explain: Q22: The diagram shows a flat barrier between top and bottom — the passage says *'a screen can be inserted between the brood chamber and the supers'*. So the answer is **screen**.

items.sentence_raw: Three weeks later the honey can be gathered.
Foul smelling chemicals are often used to irritate the bees and drive them down into the hive's bottom boxes, leaving the honey-filled supers more or less bee free.
items.explain: Q17: The passage says *'Foul smelling chemicals are often used'* to drive bees down — **'chemicals'** is the exact word from the list. So the answer is **K**.

items.sentence_raw: These can then be pulled off the hive.
They are heavy with honey and may weigh up to 90 pounds each.
The supers are taken to a warehouse.
In the extracting room, the frames are lifted out and lowered into an "uncapper" where rotating blades shave away the wax that covers each cell.
items.explain:
Q18: The passage says rotating blades shave wax from each *'cell'* — the list word **'combs'** means the whole structure made of many cells. So the answer is **M**.

Q20: The diagram shows small holes in the frame — the passage says blades shave wax that *'covers each cell'*. So the answer is **cells**.

Q21: The diagram shows the removable wooden part — the passage says *'the frames are lifted out'* for extracting. So the answer is **frames**.

items.sentence_raw: The uncapped frames are put in a carousel that sits on the bottom of a large stainless steel drum.
The carousel is filled to capacity with 72 frames.
A switch is flipped and the frames begin to whirl at 300 revolutions per minute; centrifugal force throws the honey out of the combs.
items.explain: Q27: The passage says centrifugal force *'throws the honey out of the combs'* — the spinning removes honey, it does not make it liquid. ***The honey is already liquid inside the comb*** — spinning just extracts it. So the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: Finally the honey is poured into barrels for shipment.
After this, approximately a quarter of the hives weakened by disease, mites, or an ageing or dead queen, will have to be replaced.
To create new colonies, a healthy double hive, teeming with bees, can be separated into two boxes.
items.explain: Q19: The passage says a healthy double hive can be *'separated into two boxes'* — **'separated'** means **'split'**, which is the exact word from the list. So the answer is **I**.

items.sentence_raw: One half will hold the queen and a young, already mated queen can be put in the other half, to make two hives from one.
By the time the flowers bloom, the new queens will be laying eggs, filling each hive with young worker bees.
The beekeeper's family will then migrate with them to their summer location.

orphan_explain_map.24: Q24: The passage says ancient Egyptians moved hives *'down the Nile'* on rafts — but it never says they kept bees *'on the banks'* of the Nile. ***The passage mentions the river, not the banks*** — this specific location is missing. So the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
